newsitem.title: USA: Ashland to establish group, cut expenses.
newsitem.headline: Ashland to establish group, cut expenses.

text.p: Ashland Inc said Monday that it plans to establish a petroleum group division consisting of Ashland Petroleum, SuperAmerica and Valvoline.
Ashland said in a release Monday that it will reduce capital employed in refining by cutting capital expenditures for the petroleum group to $150 million from $175 million.
Ashland said that capital expenditures for refining will be limited to $100 million, and that it will continue to explore other strategic alternatives and alliances.

Paul W. Chellgren, chief executive officer of Ashland Inc said, "Ashland's No. 1 priority is to improve returns in its refining and marketing segment. Many of the elements in the plan announced today focus on that priority and are aimed at continuing to build a basis for the long-term competitiveness of this business."
He said that the establishment of a petroleum group was in line with its priority, as well as reducing capital employed in refining.

Chellgren further stated that Ashland will continue to encourage the ongoing discussions between Ashland Coal, Inc. and Arch Mineral Corporation, in which Ashland has separate equity ownership positions. The two coal companies previously announced they are discussing a possible business combination. Chellgren said the decision to limit capital expenditures for refining to $100 million will be "well below" its annual depreciation of $22 million.
The company said the remaining $50 million in its 1997 capital budget will be earmarked for value-added petrochemical and Ashland branded marketing expansions.
Chellgren added that future capital spending for refining will remain materially less than its annual depreciation.

Chellgren also said that Ashland will review options for strategic alliances, while continuing to assess and explore options for alignments or partnering with others to enhance returns from the refining business.

Chellgren said Ashland retained CS First Boston Corporation to evaluate strategic alternatives including mergers and spin-offs, regarding Ashland Exploration, Inc. The goal is to complete an evaluation and any resulting business transaction before the end of calendar 1997, subject to regulatory approvals, tax rulings and market conditions.
